title: Custom Iterators: Fibonacci and Collatz
prompt:
Implement the Iterator trait for two structs.

1. Fib yields the Fibonacci sequence as u64: 0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, ... It must STOP (return None) instead of overflowing: after yielding the largest Fibonacci number that fits in a u64, the iterator ends. Use checked_add. Fib::new() creates a fresh iterator.

2. Collatz::new(n) yields the Collatz sequence starting at n: n, then n/2 if n is even or 3n+1 if odd, ending after it yields 1. Collatz::new(0) yields nothing.

Because these implement Iterator, all adapters (take, filter, sum, count, last...) work for free.

Example:
  Fib::new().take(7).collect::<Vec<_>>() -> [0, 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8]
  Collatz::new(6).collect::<Vec<_>>() -> [6, 3, 10, 5, 16, 8, 4, 2, 1]
